title: A counterexample to McKean's conjecture for the Landau-Coulomb equation
summary: We disprove McKean's conjecture, which asserts that the entropy dissipation is monotone nonincreasing along solutions, or equivalently that the entropy is convex in time, for the spatially homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation. We provide an explicit counterexample which consists of a Maxwellian equilibrium under radially symmetric, smooth perturbation on an annulus of scale $R\gg 1$. Developing the derivative of the entropy dissipation in powers of $R$ reveals that the leading order terms can be positive for a suitably chosen perturbation.
